newsitem.title: USA: Minnesota plans to sell $200 mln GOs in July.
newsitem.headline: Minnesota plans to sell $200 mln GOs in July.

text.p: Minnesota plans to sell about $200 million of tax-exempt general obligation state various purpose bonds on July 29, a state financial bond analyst said Friday.

Proceeds from about $15 million of the competitive sale will be used to partially fund construction of the new state Revenue Department headquarters, said Susan Gurrola, an analyst for the state Finance Department.
The remaining proceeds will be used to fund numerous projects ranging from transportation to pollution control, Gurrola said.
The bonds will be dated August 1 and Minnesota expects to close on the paperwork on August 19, Gurrola said.
Minnesota also plans to sell $14 million of taxable general obligation bonds competitively on July 30 for the state's rural finance authority program and railroad transportation plan, Gurrola said.
Dorsey & Whitney LLP of Minneapolis will serve as bond counsel to both the issues, Gurrola said. Minnesota has obtained no financial adviser for the sales, she added.
Minnesota is also considering another issuance of tax-exempt and taxable general obligation debt in spring 1998 in excess of $100 million, Gurrola said.
